title: Calls: Co-op Cattle Trucks and Elementary School Parents

callee.name: TCEMA EOC Duty Desk
callee.label: Tallis County EOC, Courthouse annex, Cedar Ford

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: Tallis County Emergency Management, EOC duty desk.

transcript.speaker: Co-op GM
transcript.text: Morning. This is Ellen Strand at Tallis Prairie Co-op, down at the river bend on 38. I need the Coordinator if I can get him. I've got 340 head in the feed yard, and the anhydrous tanks at the fertilizer plant.

transcript.speaker: Co-op GM
transcript.text: The yard goes under at 19 feet. It takes me 24 hours and 14 cattle trucks to get that herd up to the Weller farm. The truckers want a firm answer by noon, or they book other loads.

transcript.speaker: Co-op GM
transcript.text: Your warning says 18.2. So... do I move or not? Give me a stage and a time I can plan on.

transcript.speaker: Co-op GM
transcript.text: Okay. And if they bump that number up tonight, how fast am I going to hear about it? Because by then I've lost my trucks. Who calls me?

transcript.speaker: Co-op GM
transcript.text: All right. I'll be at the office line all morning. Noon's my deadline, I mean it.

transcript.speaker: Recorder
transcript.text: Next call. 06:35, from 319-555-0142, Tallis Elementary School.

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: Tallis County Emergency Management, EOC duty desk.

transcript.speaker: Principal
transcript.text: Hi, this is the principal over at Tallis Elementary. I'm sorry to call so early. Parents are already going back and forth on the school text thread about whether we close this week.

transcript.speaker: Principal
transcript.text: One dad keeps posting that the river always goes over the levee in April, and now other parents are asking me if they should keep their kids home.

transcript.speaker: Principal
transcript.text: What should I tell them? And when will we actually know?

transcript.speaker: Principal
transcript.text: Can you put that in an email I can forward to the families? I'd rather send them something from you than from me.

voiceStyles.TCEMA: Calm, neutral duty desk voice, early-morning office
voiceStyles.Co-op GM: Man in his 50s, rural Iowa, blunt and impatient, phone in a pickup cab
voiceStyles.Principal: Woman in her 40s, polite but worried, speaking fast, quiet school office

instructorNote: This is a pressure inject. Watch whether the EM quotes the current forecast exactly (05:15 issuance, 18.2 ft at 06:00 Friday, minor, below the 19.0 ft yard level) without promising the crest will hold. The EM should advise the co-op to book trucks and secure the anhydrous tanks now, given its long lead time and forecasts that keep changing. The PIO should add both callers to the partner contact list, log the levee rumor, and give the school a factual note: levee crest at 26.0 ft on the gauge, no closure at the current forecast, issuance named.
